steps: Title globe: picked Ceasefire or Collapse, then Ukraine
Read briefing, took office as Zelensky
Chose 'Only by referendum' on the US peace map, offered Putin talks on a ceasefire
Handled assassination attempt, Belarus hostages (negotiated), blackout winter (rationed and appealed to Europe), US offer, grid down
Read debriefs and the Chronicle each month
Page froze around month 7 and never recovered
scenarios.notes: Leaders were right (Zelensky, Putin, Macron, Merz, Takaichi, Frederiksen). UK PM Andy Burnham I could not verify and would fact-check. Never reached the verdict.

steps: Read the effect arrows on every crisis option before choosing
Opened the Putin call and compared three replies
Looked in the debriefs for what really happened
scenarios.notes: Choices explain what they do (arrows, who backs it, mission warning). No real-world context in debriefs or Chronicle, so the learning half of my goal is unmet.

friction.where: Debrief tabs (Diplomacy, Home and security) and Next button
friction.happened: Only a raw screen tap worked at the bottom-right Next button; clicking tab labels did nothing in the driver

friction.expected: What happened to my country that month
friction.happened: Same 'Reform program' card and the same two bullets (war weariness, shrinking economy) every month; I stopped reading it

friction.expected: A line about why the crisis outcome happened, tied to real events
friction.happened: Generic template: 'On blackout winter, President Zelensky decided: Ration and appeal to Europe', with an Interior ministry quote about losing districts that does not fit a power cut. Same boardroom picture every month.

friction.expected: Delta chips match the before and after
friction.happened: Stability 51.1 -> 51.1 shows +6; Reform shows 1.9 -> 2 +0.1; front 47 -> 47 shows +1. Rounding makes the arrows look wrong.
Crisis card says stability 56.5 -> 48.5 (-8) while the month tile says -2.9; I did not know which was real
Court United Kingdom and National address / Reform program were pre-queued by staff every month; I never chose them and wasn't told what they were for until the debrief
Clicking the option text often did not register until I tapped the card again; I had to verify with a screenshot
Page stopped responding (screenshots, reload both time out)

bugs.title: Page freezes and cannot be reloaded around month 7
steps: Play Ukraine Flashpoint, execute month 6 via staff picks
bugs.actual: Execute month clicks time out, then screenshot and goto time out; tab dead. Machine was under heavy load (GPU process using about 4 cores), so may be rendering cost of the animated scenes rather than a logic bug.

bugs.title: Crisis reaction quote does not fit the crisis
steps: Choose Ration and appeal to Europe in Blackout winter
bugs.actual: Interior ministry: We are losing control of several districts

bugs.title: Crisis headline calls the player's own choice 'Zelensky on X: Y' and labels it Crisis, Germany or United States
steps: Finish a crisis, read month page
bugs.expected: Neutral headline and my country as subject
bugs.actual: Tag shows other country, headline reads as a stilted template

suggestions.what: Add a short 'What really happened' box to each debrief and crisis outcome that names the real Nov 2026 event, with a source line
Make the Home and security page report different things each month instead of repeating the reform card; explain staff orders when queued
Show the real-world leader list for the scenario on the title dossier so a student can check it in five seconds
Reduce animation cost (or offer a low motion mode) so the game does not freeze on weaker machines

delight: Every crisis option lists its effects with arrows and who backs it before I commit (007-desk.png)
Briefing text is sharp and plausible: Washington pushing a map, half the grid gone, Patriots vs oil above $100 (030-a5.png)
The globe title with all 8 live flashpoints and the 'today' crisis (001-title.png)
Putin call with a quote and a front-line gauge felt like a real negotiation (014-d1.png)

fun.reason: The crises were interesting and I wanted to see the next one, but the monthly loop of approve-all-and-execute became rote by month 4.

clarity.reason: Option effects are explained before choosing, which is exactly what I want; the debrief numbers contradict each other in places.

visual.reason: Title globe and scene art look good; the same boardroom picture repeats and the Chronicle is bland.

feels_like_a_game.reason: Feels like a polished briefing tool; staff pre-fill makes decisions feel done for me.

agency.reason: I never hit an opaque refusal, which was my deal breaker. Staff picks and pre-queued orders blurred what I chose.

realism.reason: Zelensky, Putin, Macron, Merz, Takaichi all right; Burnham as UK PM I could not confirm; the debrief text is generic and gives no real context.

replay.reason: I would try Taiwan or Hormuz once, but nothing told me what really happened, so my learning goal is only half served.

recommend.reason: I would not yet tell my Model UN club: promising decisions UI, but no real-world debriefs and the page froze on me.

quit_point: Month 7 of 12 in Ceasefire or Collapse: Execute month stopped responding and the tab would not reload; before that I had already stopped reading the repetitive Home and security page.
verbatim: The choices explain themselves and the leaders are right, but tell me what really happened, because that is why I came.
